text:
[name]
[email] [phone] Minneapolis, MN

I am a laboratory manager with six years of full-time experience in two university biology laboratories, currently at the University of Minnesota in a developmental biology group and previously at Iowa State University in a plant genetics group. I hold a master's degree in biology from Iowa State University, completed in 2020, and a bachelor's degree in biology from the University of Northern Iowa, completed in 2018. My master's thesis concerned the regulation of root hair development in Arabidopsis under phosphate limitation and was supported by a departmental teaching assistantship for two years.

Since August 2023 I have managed the day-to-day operation of a developmental biology laboratory at the University of Minnesota with a principal investigator, two postdoctoral researchers, five graduate students and a rotating group of three to five undergraduates. In that role I order and track supplies against an annual operating budget of roughly $180,000, maintain the laboratory's zebrafish colony of about 2,400 fish across 160 tanks together with a part-time animal technician, write and update the standard operating procedures and the chemical hygiene plan, schedule and train new members on confocal microscopy, and act as the laboratory's safety officer for inspections by the university's environmental health and safety office, which the laboratory has passed with no citations in each of the last three years. I also carry out my own experiments, mostly CRISPR mutagenesis and in situ hybridization, and I contributed the genotyping and imaging for a paper published in Developmental Biology in 2025 on which I am the fourth of seven authors. I supervised two undergraduate honors theses in 2024 and 2025, both of which were completed and defended.

From June 2020 to July 2023 I was the laboratory manager and research technician in a plant genetics group at Iowa State University, where I had done my master's work. The group had one principal investigator, three graduate students and two undergraduates. I ran the growth chambers and the greenhouse space allocated to the group, maintained the seed stock collection of about 1,100 lines, performed DNA extraction and PCR genotyping for roughly 6,000 samples a year, and managed the ordering and the equipment service contracts. I trained seven graduate and undergraduate students on genotyping and plant care. I was the third of five authors on a paper in Plant Physiology in 2022 that reported a transcription factor involved in the phosphate starvation response, for which I generated the mutant lines and performed the phenotyping. Between 2018 and 2020, while completing the master's degree, I was a teaching assistant for introductory biology laboratories for four semesters, leading two sections of about 24 students each term.

My technical skills include CRISPR/Cas9 mutagenesis, PCR and qPCR, cloning, in situ hybridization, immunohistochemistry, confocal and widefield fluorescence microscopy, zebrafish and Arabidopsis husbandry, basic statistics in R, and image analysis in ImageJ and Fiji. I have presented posters at the Midwest Zebrafish Meeting in 2024 and at the Plant Biology annual meeting in 2021. I am interested in a senior laboratory manager or research specialist position, and I would consider a staff scientist role in a core facility.
